Advent Sunday Sausage and Egg Bake

Served at: Second Sunday of Advent

Serves 6-8Prep 20 minCook 45-55 min

This comforting sausage and egg bake is a perfect dish for the Second Sunday of Advent, offering a warm and satisfying start to a day of reflection and anticipation. Its make-ahead nature allows for more precious family time on a busy Sunday morning during the holiday season, embodying the spirit of preparation and togetherness.

Ingredients

  • 1 lb (450g) bulk breakfast sausage
  • 6 slices day-old bread, crusts removed and cubed (about 4 cups)
  • 1 cup (120g) shredded sharp cheddar cheese
  • 8 large eggs
  • 2 cups (480ml) whole milk
  • 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • Optional: 1/2 cup (75g) chopped green bell pepper
  • Optional: 1/4 cup (40g) chopped yellow onion

Method

  1. Lightly grease a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking dish.
  2. In a large skillet over medium heat, cook the breakfast sausage, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Drain any excess grease.
  3. If using, add the chopped bell pepper and onion to the skillet with the cooked sausage and sauté for 3-5 minutes until softened.
  4. Spread the cubed bread evenly in the bottom of the prepared baking dish.
  5. Sprinkle the cooked sausage and vegetable mixture over the bread cubes, then top evenly with the shredded cheddar cheese.
  6. In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper until well combined.
  7. Pour the egg mixture evenly over the ingredients in the baking dish, ensuring the bread is well-saturated.
  8. Cover the dish with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the bread to soak up the egg mixture.
  9. When ready to bake, preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Remove the casserole from the refrigerator and let it sit at room temperature for 15-20 minutes.
  10. Bake, uncovered, for 45-55 minutes, or until the casserole is set in the center and lightly golden brown on top.
  11. Let stand for 5-10 minutes before serving to allow it to set further.

Tips

  • For a vegetarian option, omit the sausage and add 1 cup of sautéed mushrooms, spinach, or extra bell peppers.
  • Experiment with different cheeses like Monterey Jack, Gruyere, or a blend of your favorites for varied flavor.
  • This casserole can be assembled the night before, making Sunday morning preparations effortless and allowing more time for Advent reflections.
